analytic_reference.coordinate_note: G is invariant under orthogonal similarity transformations but can change under arbitrary state rescaling.
analytic_reference.maximum: Maximum over the explicitly sampled time grid, not a continuous-time maximizer.
analytic_reference.propagator: P_kappa(t)=[[exp(-a*t), kappa*(exp(-a*t)-exp(-b*t))/(b-a)],[0,exp(-b*t)]] for a != b; P_0 is diagonal.

design_gate.norm: Euclidean vector norm; induced matrix 2-norm (largest singular value). Not energy or a physical magnitude.
design_gate.permitted_coordinate_changes: Orthogonal changes of basis only; arbitrary rescaling and nonorthogonal similarity changes are outside the declared metric.
design_gate.physical_claim: None; no physical system mapping is asserted.
design_gate.state: Two abstract dimensionless coordinates x1,x2 in R^2, each normalized as a coefficient on an orthonormal unit basis direction with equal scale.

hypotheses_and_decisions.H1_finite_time_amplification: Supported if any nonzero kappa has a sampled positive-time G(t)>1.01 on both primary and refined grids. Not supported if none does. Inconclusive if grid resolution fails or required gain values are nonfinite.
hypotheses_and_decisions.H2_exceeds_matched_normal: Supported if any nonzero kappa has sampled full-horizon maximum gain at least 0.01 above the normal baseline on both grids. Not supported if none does. Inconclusive if resolution check fails.
hypotheses_and_decisions.H3_numerical_agreement: Supported if all required integrations succeed and all trajectory errors are <=1e-8, propagator cross-checks <=1e-12, and resolution limits are met. Not supported if an integration fails or exceeds tolerance; report each failed condition without dropping it.
hypotheses_and_decisions.normal_baseline: Its sampled gain must never exceed 1+1e-12; otherwise implementation/check fails.
hypotheses_and_decisions.zero_coupling: kappa=0 analytic gain curves must match A0 within 1e-14.

assumptions: Euclidean norm in declared orthonormal basis
model.coupling_grid_rationale: The separate design_exploration.json uses only the exact triangular propagator and SVD. It includes zero, a below-threshold case, and cases above the 0.01 gain-effect threshold; the compact grid was selected before primary evaluation.
model.eigenvalues: -a and -b, exactly matched; both negative for a,b>0.
model.normality: A0 is normal; A_kappa is non-normal for kappa != 0.
model.time: Dimensionless tau=t/t_ref; A entries are dimensionless rates per unit tau.

protocol.baseline: A0 with same a,b; its induced 2-norm is max(exp(-a*t),exp(-b*t)) and is at most 1, with grid maximum 1 at t=0.
protocol.horizon_rationale: Four decay times of the slow eigenmode a=1 leave exp(-4) of its asymptotic component; this includes early growth and substantial late decay.
protocol.independent_propagator_check: Compare closed-form P(t) against scipy.linalg.expm(A*t) for all kappa at fixed times 0, 0.37, 1.2, and 4, tolerance 1e-12 in max absolute entry.

numerical_comparisons.initial_condition: leading right singular vector at the sampled maximum (coordinate e1 at t=0)
leading right singular vector at the primary sampled maximum
leading right singular vector at the primary sampled maximum
coordinate vector e2, as a non-optimal-direction diagnostic

protocol.optimal_initial_direction: Use the leading right singular vector of P(t_peak) on the primary grid; make its largest-magnitude component positive to fix the otherwise arbitrary sign.
primary_outcomes: sampled-horizon maximum gain relative to matched normal baseline
protocol.semigroup_check: Check max absolute entry of P(s+t)-P(s)P(t) at frozen pairs (0.2,0.7), (0.8,1.1), tolerance 1e-12.
protocol.threshold_rationale: An absolute gain increase of 0.01 is a predeclared 1% change relative to a unit-norm initial perturbation; it is an operational descriptive threshold, not a universal physical threshold.
protocol.tighter_solver_conditions: Repeat optimal initial directions at kappa=4 and 8.
protocol.trajectory_error_metric: Maximum over output times of the Euclidean norm of numerical state minus analytic P(t)x0.

reproducibility.manifest: SHA-256 for all files in this report output directory except the manifest itself.
reproducibility.rerun: Copy design_exploration.json and protocol.json into an empty isolated directory; run the study there and compare every manifested output hash.

research_question: Can a stable non-normal system exhibit greater finite-time amplification than a normal system with the same eigenvalues under a declared state norm and finite horizon?
stopping_criteria: Stop after all four frozen kappa values, prescribed solver comparisons, and numerical checks are reported.
If required checks fail, report the affected result as unresolved and diagnose only the specific failure; do not widen the matrix/coupling/horizon design to obtain a preferred result.
Do not extend the matrix family or claim physical/cross-domain validation.
